The description of the Sub over at Reddit was "news for genome hackers", and we had a great array of information in the sidebar and "Learning Bioinformatics" section, but largely the information was for learning genomics. Since Bioinformatics is really such a broad field, including - my interests - biophysics, structural biology, proteomics, as well as everything from quantum biophysics to global epidemiology and biostats, I'd request that while structuring this subverse we provide educational materials on more than genomics and structural biology in the "Learn Biology" section.

Thanks so much for creating this Subverse.
Could I make a request for this new subverse?
That is a good suggestion, bioinformatics is really broad. My program covers sooooo many!

I'd be tickled to see more than just genomics here! I'm in genomics myself, but one of the forces that led me in the direction of bioinformatics initially was an interest in protein folding.

I think the difficult part is that so many people struggle to succinctly define bioinformatics- I think of it simply as the use of information systems to study biological problems- and those systems are useful for many more biological problems than just genetics! Will you head up that effort, MixTapes? :) (that is, beginning to develop broader content for a wiki, or whatever form our supplementary materials end up taking here at voat)

The way I see it, the primary ingredient for any successful community is people willing to find and discuss content- we're in the experimental stage, you're the first new moderator of this place, any powers you need or changes you desire to make, shoot me a message, and I'll see what I can do! :)

I would love to learn more about epidemiology. I'm reading Richard Preston's The Demon in the Freezer now, I got into a hobby of learning about viruses after reading his book on ebola, The Hot Zone. Fascinating history.

Personally, I'm also interested in learning about how Bioinformatics can be applied to gain insights about how the mind works--and what works differently in individuals with things like ADHD, anxiety, depression, schizophrenia, and so on. I suppose that's called psychiatric genomics.
